limitations: Manifest declarations are direct requests, not installed resolutions; compiler edges include observed modules/types/path references, not the full runtime/transitive package graph.

Inventoried package.json files are package candidates, not proof of pnpm workspace-glob membership. Exotic manifests, custom stores, PnP loaders, hooks and unobserved runtime imports are not interpreted or executed.
Lock/install metadata is fingerprinted, not parsed or verified against node_modules. Branch/custom lockfiles and non-ancestor user/global configuration are not exhaustively discovered.

Equal content digests do not merge package instances or authorize semantic reuse. Source projects are conservative affected consumers; source consumers are direct edges, not a complete invalidation closure.

Memberships bind program participation and redirect roles to project/options contexts, not successful checking or build execution. Context hashes alone are not complete reusable dependency identities.

SHA-256 identifies compiler-decoded text (virtual text for framework blocks), not archive integrity or raw file encoding. Default compiler libraries are omitted from this graph but their observed reads remain in the gate snapshot.
Compiler checking and selected bounded behavioral rules do not prove runtime correctness or Rust behavioral-rule parity.
Source/configuration/dependency observations were revalidated before return, not atomically locked against subsequent changes.
Inventory excludes dependency, configured output and cache directories. Symlinks/junctions are not traversed and make coverage incomplete.
ASAR members are outside this filesystem/compiler scope. Explicit javascript_coverage archives supplies evidence only, not packaged-source semantic analysis.

Local declarations skipped by skipLibCheck, suppressions, unchecked/excluded source and unlowered framework semantics make coverage incomplete. Framework scripts use host-owned parsers; templates, macros, reactivity and component lifetimes remain unknown.

EJS default-delimiter projections preserve cross-tag syntax and conditional facts, not render-option/locals/include/encoding semantics. EJS behavioral findings are withheld; ERB requires a Ruby provider. Literal emitted scripts are not server JavaScript.

limitations: Findings prove the stated structural rule violation, not runtime reachability or a concurrent writer.
Function bodies are analyzed as entrypoints; implicit exceptions, dynamic dispatch, arbitrary loops and framework lifetimes are not proven.
Promise handling transfers rejection responsibility; a handler is not proof of application-level recovery.
Node scheduling order, module evaluation, loader hooks and runtime export conditions are not simulated; compiler resolution is not proof of runtime module identity.
